CalibrationDiagnostics.description:
Calibration diagnostics providing condition number, residual analysis, and fit quality.

These diagnostics are only populated when `CalibrationConfig::compute_diagnostics`
is set to `true`. They are relatively expensive to compute (requiring Jacobian
analysis) and are intended for calibration debugging, auditing, and quality
monitoring rather than production hot paths.

condition_number.description:
Condition number of the weighted Jacobian's normal equations (J^T * W * J).
`W` contains the configured residual weights; unweighted fits use identity.

A high condition number (e.g., > 1e10) indicates an ill-conditioned
calibration problem where small changes in market data can produce
large changes in calibrated parameters.

jacobian.description:
Finite-difference Jacobian of the residuals at the solution.

`jacobian[i][j]` is the derivative of the residual of quote `i` with
respect to solved parameter `j`: rows follow [`Self::per_quote`] order,
columns follow the solved parameters in knot order (for curve targets,
the knot values at increasing knot times). Entries are in the report's
residual units per unit of the solved parameter, and are unweighted;
[`Self::condition_number`] is computed from this matrix with the
residual weights applied. `per_quote[i].sensitivity` equals
`max_j |jacobian[i][j]|`.

Present only for global (simultaneous) solves in which every parameter
bump could be priced. Absent for sequential bootstraps, which solve one
knot per quote and build no full Jacobian.

max_residual.description: Maximum absolute residual across all quotes.

per_quote.description: Per-quote quality metrics for each calibration instrument.

rms_residual.description: Root mean square residual across all quotes.

convergence_reason.description: Human-readable reason for convergence or failure.

diagnostics.description:
Optional calibration diagnostics (condition number, per-quote quality, etc.).

Only populated when `CalibrationConfig::compute_diagnostics` is `true`.
Provides detailed information about the quality and stability of the
calibration for debugging, auditing, and monitoring purposes.

explanation.description: Optional detailed trace of the calibration steps (enabled via config).

fitted_slices.description:
Smile parameters fitted per quoted expiry, in increasing expiry order.

Populated by the equity SABR (`vol_surface`) and SVI (`svi_surface`)
surface calibrators, whose gridded output surface does not retain the
fitted parameters. Empty for every other calibrator, including the
swaption SABR cube, which stores its node parameters on the cube.

iterations.description: Number of solver iterations or function evaluations.

max_residual.description:
Maximum absolute residual across all instruments, in the residual
units of the calibrator that produced this report (raw units for a
step report; the largest step `max_residual` for a plan report).

max_residual_ratio.description:
Plan-level only: maximum `|residual| / step_tolerance` ratio across
every quote of every step. `None` on per-step reports.

model_version.description:
Optional model/methodology version used for this calibration.

Used for audit trails and regulatory compliance. Examples:
- "ISDA Standard Model v1.8.2" for CDS hazard curve calibration
- "Multi-curve OIS discounting" for discount curve calibration
- "SABR v1.0" for volatility surface calibration

residual_units.description:
Units of [`Self::residuals`], [`Self::max_residual`] and [`Self::rmse`].

Set by every calibrator in this crate. `None` on reports built directly
through [`Self::new`] or `Self::for_type_with_tolerance` without a solver.
Missing units are unknown; metadata does not supply a fallback.

residuals.description: Final residuals (fitting errors) by instrument identifier.

rmse.description:
Root mean square error of all residuals, in the same units as
[`Self::max_residual`].

rmse_ratio.description:
Plan-level only: root mean square of `|residual| / step_tolerance`
across every quote of every step. `None` on per-step reports.

solver_config.description: Solver configuration used during this calibration run.

solver_method.description:
Numerical procedure that produced this report.

Set by every calibrator in this crate. `None` only on reports built
directly through [`Self::new`] or `Self::for_type_with_tolerance`
without a solver.

success.description: User-facing success flag. True only if both fitting and validation passed.

success_tolerance.description:
Configured tolerance used to determine [`Self::success`] from residuals.

Set by `Self::for_type_with_tolerance`; `None` for reports built via [`Self::new`]
directly (no tolerance gate applied). This is the typed source of truth for the
success-gate tolerance; it is distinct from `solver_config.tolerance()`, which controls
when the numerical root-finder stops.

validation_passed.description: Whether the calibrated market object passed all validation checks.

worst_quote_id.description:
Identifier of the quote with the largest absolute residual.

Derived from `residuals`. `None` only when `residuals` is empty. This
is the quote a user should look at first when a step fails to
converge — the input most likely to fix.

DividendKind.description:
Type of dividend event.

Distinguishes between cash payments, stock distributions, and continuous
yield approximations used in different pricing models.

# Variants

- **Cash**: Actual dividend payment (quarterly, semi-annual, etc.)
- **Stock**: Share distribution (less common, complicates option pricing)
- **Yield**: Continuous approximation for analytical models

oneOf.description:
Cash dividend payment.

Most common type. Ex-dividend date reduces stock price by dividend amount.

Continuous dividend yield (annualized fraction).

Used in analytical models (Black-Scholes with dividends) that assume
continuous payout rather than discrete payments.

Stock dividend (share distribution).

Increases share count proportionally. For example, 5% stock dividend
means each shareholder receives 0.05 additional shares per share held.

ratio.description: Stock distribution ratio; 0.05 corresponds to a 5% stock dividend.

currency.description: Quote currency for cash dividends (optional metadata).

id.description: Unique identifier of this schedule in the market context.

ExplanationTrace.description:
Container for detailed execution traces of financial computations.

Traces are organized by type (calibration, pricing, waterfall) and contain
a sequence of domain-specific entries. Traces can be serialized to JSON for
inspection, debugging, or audit purposes.

Mutation is intentionally single-threaded through `&mut self`. If multiple
workers need to append to one trace, wrap it in external synchronization and
keep ordering semantics explicit at the call site.

truncated.description: Whether the trace was truncated due to size limits

ExtrapolationPolicy.description:
Extrapolation policy for evaluation outside the knot range.

Every interpolation strategy honours this policy at both ends of the knot
range. Callers must choose an explicit policy:

- `Flat`: hold the boundary ordinate constant outside the knot range
  (and return derivative `0.0` strictly outside the knot range).
- `Extend`: extend the boundary segment's slope in the interpolation style's
  working space (table below).
- `Error`: refuse to extrapolate; return an explicit error for queries
  outside `[knots[0], knots[last]]`.

What `Extend` extends depends on the [`InterpStyle`]:

| Style | `Extend` extends | On a discount-factor curve | On a rate-valued curve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | the value linearly | - | rates keep trending |
| `CubicHermite` | the value linearly, with the end-knot slope | - | rates keep trending |
| `LogLinear` | `ln(value)` linearly | flat forward rate | - |
| `PiecewiseQuadraticForward` | `ln(value)` linearly | flat forward rate | - |
| `MonotoneConvex` | the boundary instantaneous forward | flat forward rate | - |

The market-standard tail for a discount-factor curve is a flat forward
rate (`Extend` with a log-space style). For a curve that stores rates or
spreads, holding the last rate constant is `Flat`.

oneOf.description: Hold the boundary value constant outside `[knots[0], knots[last]]`.

Extend the boundary segment's slope in the interpolation style's
working space; see the table on [`ExtrapolationPolicy`].
Return an error for queries outside `[knots[0], knots[last]]`.

FittedSlice.description:
Parameters a surface calibrator fitted to the quotes of one expiry.

The SABR and SVI surface calibrators fit one smile per quoted expiry and
then sample those smiles onto the surface's target grid. The gridded
surface keeps only the sampled volatilities, so the fitted parameters are
recorded here, one entry per quoted expiry in increasing expiry order.

expiry.description:
Expiry of the quotes this slice was fitted to, as an Act/365F year
fraction from the calibration base date. This is a quoted expiry, not
necessarily a node of the surface's target expiry grid.

iterations.description:
Solver iterations spent on this slice (all attempted starts for SABR).
The slice iterations sum to [`CalibrationReport::iterations`].

max_relative_quote_error.description:
Largest `|model − market| / market` volatility error of the fitted
smile over this slice's quotes, as a decimal fraction of the quoted
volatility (`1e-4` is 0.01%). It measures the smile fit itself; the
report's residuals measure the gridded surface instead.

Present for SABR slices. Absent for SVI slices, whose fit reports no
per-slice error.

parameters.description: Fitted model parameters for this expiry.

FittedSliceParameters.description:
Smile-model parameters fitted to one expiry slice of a volatility surface.

The wire form is externally tagged by model: `{"sabr": {...}}` or
`{"svi": {...}}`.

oneOf.description:
SABR parameters (`alpha`, `beta`, `nu`, `rho` and the optional
displacement `shift`).

Raw SVI total-variance parameters (`a`, `b`, `rho`, `m`, `sigma`) in
log-moneyness `ln(K / F)`.

ForwardCurveTransform.description:
Source interpolation and a single accumulated transformation, never a chain
of nested curves. The adjustment is stored as its piecewise-linear derivative
so evaluating beyond a completed triangular shock does not subtract large
quadratic polynomials.

adjustment.description: Cumulative derivative of the additive log-factor adjustment.

source_base_date.description: Original, untransformed curve base date defining the source coordinate system.

cache_capacity.description: Maximum number of provider-observed quotes retained in the LRU cache.

pivot_currency.description:
Single pivot for `from -> pivot -> to` cross routing, or `None` for
direct quotes only. Required on the wire (`null` disables routing).

Only this one pivot is tried: no alternative pivot, multi-hop search or
market-order inference. A pair whose market convention routes through
another currency needs its direct quote seeded explicitly.

FxConversionPolicy.description:
Provider-selection purpose of a point-date FX query (record
CORE-CONVENTIONS-013 #1/#2).

The policy tells a provider which source purpose the rate serves; it does
not calculate dates or choose spot versus forward. There is no default:
every query names its policy. Period averages are not point queries; an
owner that needs one computes the oriented aggregate itself.

oneOf.description: The rate applicable on a cashflow's own date.
The rate applicable on a reporting period's closing date.

atm_vols.description: ATM delta-neutral straddle vols per expiry.

pair.description: Currency pair (`base/quote`) matching quoted FX forward orientation.

FxMatrixState.description:
Serializable state of an FxMatrix.
Contains the configuration and cached quotes that can be persisted and restored.
Serialization fails with an ordinary serializer error if any captured
explicit or provider rate is non-finite or non-positive, including rates
that overflow after a mutable underlying provider changes under a shock.

pinned_quotes.description:
Pinned, date/policy-scoped quotes as `(from, to, on, policy, rate)`.

Required: a snapshot that omits it would silently re-derive those
dates from the provider instead of restoring the pinned fixings.

Captured date/policy-scoped provider quotes. These override captured
pair-global provider quotes for their scope while remaining below
explicit matrix quotes in either direction. Required even when empty.

provider_quotes.description:
Captured provider quotes, below explicit global and date/policy-pinned
quotes in lookup priority. Market-context restoration uses these to
rebuild a quote-only provider; arbitrary live provider behavior is not
serialized. Required even when the provider has no snapshot quotes.

Exact valuation-layer inputs required to replay a hazard-curve calibration.

The core market-data crate stores these payloads without interpreting them;
the calibration crate deserializes them back into its canonical
`HazardCurveParams`, typed CDS quotes, and `CalibrationConfig`. Keeping the
complete serde payloads avoids replacing date pillars with rounded tenors or
silently substituting current defaults for the original solver policy.

integrates directly on the retained source timeline.

MarketDataHierarchy.description:
Top-level market-data hierarchy containing ordered root entries.

Each root represents a major organizational branch (such as `"Rates"`,
`"Credit"`, `"FX"`, `"Equity"`, or `"Volatility"`). Roots and child levels
use explicit name/node entry arrays so numeric-looking names retain their
authored sequence across Rust, Python, and JavaScript.

MarketDataTarget.description:
Canonical family-typed identifier for an addressable entry in
[`MarketContext`](crate::market_data::context::MarketContext).

Identifiers in `MarketContext` are namespace-local: the same `CurveId` may
coexist across distinct stores (for example a `VolSurface` and a
`ScalarTimeSeries`). `MarketDataTarget` pairs an exact [`CurveId`] with the
exact store and subkind to select without multi-store probing.

Linear interpolation between observed points

max_iterations.description: Positive maximum number of iterations available to each solver invocation.

tolerance.description: Positive finite numerical convergence tolerance, distinct from economic fit acceptance.

SolverMethod.description:
Numerical procedure that produced a [`CalibrationReport`].

The wire form is the snake_case variant name (for example
`"sequential_bootstrap"`).

oneOf.description:
Knots solved one at a time in maturity order, each by a bracketed
one-dimensional root find on its own quote (curve bootstraps and the
piecewise Hull-White volatility bootstrap).

All parameters solved simultaneously by weighted Levenberg-Marquardt
least squares over every quote.

One independent least-squares smile fit per expiry (or per
expiry/tenor bucket), as used by the SABR and SVI surface calibrators.

A single scalar parameter solved by a bracketed one-dimensional root
find (Student-t degrees of freedom).

A single scalar parameter solved by one-dimensional minimisation of
the sum of squared pricing errors (Hull-White volatility at a fixed
mean reversion).

Aggregation of the step reports of a calibration plan; no solver ran
at this level.

generic_epsilon.description:
Epsilon for generic floating-point comparisons (default: 1e-10).

Used for general numerical comparisons where higher tolerance is acceptable.

TraceEntry.description:
Domain-specific trace entry types.

Each variant captures relevant details for different types of computations:
- Calibration: solver steps as generic computation steps
- Pricing: cashflow-level PV breakdowns
- Waterfall: step-by-step payment allocations

oneOf.description: Cashflow present value breakdown

cashflow_amount.description: Cashflow amount (stored as f64 for JSON simplicity)

survival_probability.description:
Conditional survival probability to the payment date, `S(date) / S(as_of)`.

Present only for credit-risky valuations. `pv_amount` then also
includes the recovery leg, so it is not `cashflow_amount ×
discount_factor × survival_probability`.

oneOf.description: Generic computation step (extensible)

VolCube.description:
SABR volatility cube on an expiry x tenor grid.

Each grid node stores a [`SabrParameterData`] and a forward rate. The
interpolation mode records how a models-layer evaluator should combine
nodes; core performs structural validation only.

expiries.description: Option expiries in years, strictly increasing. Indexes the first axis.

id.description: Identifier the cube is registered and looked up under.

interpolation_mode.description: How volatilities are interpolated between the cube's grid points.

tenors.description:
Underlying swap tenors in years, strictly increasing. Indexes the
second axis.

oneOf.description:
Interpolate implied volatility directly.

This is the literal choice when market quotes are given as implied
volatilities on the stored grid and you want local interpolation in
quote space.

# ⚠️ Not calendar-arbitrage-safe across expiry

Linear-in-vol interpolation along the **expiry** axis does not preserve
monotonicity of total variance `σ²·t`, so an off-grid vol read between
two expiry pillars can imply *decreasing* total variance with time —
i.e. calendar arbitrage — even when the pillar grid is itself
arbitrage-free. For arbitrage-sensitive workflows (Dupire local vol,
no-arb checks, term-structure interpolation) select
[`TotalVariance`](Self::TotalVariance) via
[`VolSurfaceBuilder::interpolation_mode`].

Interpolate total variance `sigma^2 * t`, then convert back to implied vol.

Preferred when blending across expiries: total variance behaves more
linearly in time and preserves the no-arbitrage intuition for variance
accumulation, avoiding the calendar-arbitrage trap of linear-in-vol
interpolation (see [`Vol`](Self::Vol)).

VolQuoteType.description:
Quoting convention of the volatilities stored on a [`VolSurface`].

The same `vol_surface_id` channel is read by consumers with very different
expectations: rates calibrations typically read normal (Bachelier, absolute)
vols on an `expiry × tenor` ATM matrix, while equity/FX/swaption smile
consumers read Black (lognormal, relative) vols on `expiry × strike`. The
stored numbers are an order of magnitude apart (e.g. 0.008 normal vs 0.20
Black), so misreading one as the other silently mis-prices. Tagging the
quote type lets consumers enforce their convention via
[`VolSurface::require_quote_type`].

oneOf.description: Black (lognormal) implied volatility in relative units per square-root source year.
Displaced Black volatility; one per-expiry displacement accompanies the grid.
Normal (Bachelier) implied volatility in underlying units per square-root source year.

VolSurface.description:
Volatility surface defined on an expiry × secondary-coordinate grid.

Internally stores annual volatilities in row-major order as a boxed slice.

displacements.description: Additive displacements in forward/strike units, one per expiry for shifted Black quotes.

expiries.description: Strictly positive option expiry times in years.

expiry_clock.description: Optional calibration clock mapping calendar dates to source expiry year fractions.

secondary_axis.description: Semantic meaning of the secondary axis.

secondary_values.description: Secondary-axis coordinates (absolute strikes or positive underlying tenors).

VolSurfaceAxis.description:
Semantic meaning of the secondary axis on a [`VolSurface`].

Most option surfaces are defined on `expiry × strike`, but some calibration
workflows materialize ATM matrices on `expiry × tenor`. Keeping the axis type
explicit prevents consumers from accidentally interpreting tenor buckets as
strikes.

oneOf.description: The secondary axis is literal absolute strike in underlying units.
The secondary axis is strictly positive swap or reference tenor in years.

day_count.description: Day-count convention used to measure expiry times from `reference_date`.

reference_date.description: Valuation reference date anchored to year fraction `0.0`.
